notes.statement: Russell et al. (2007) made Tectb-null mice by deleting exons 1-4. Tectb protein was absent from the tectorial membrane, and the striated-sheet matrix was missing along its whole length. The tectorial membrane stayed attached to the organ of Corti, but Hensen's stripe was absent, the marginal band was lost apically, and the apical tectorial membrane was about twice as thick as in controls.
quotes: Transmission electron microscopy revealed a complete absence of striated-sheet matrix throughout the length of the tectorial membrane in Tectb−/− mutant mice
there was a noticeable absence of Hensen’s stripe, a longitudinal ridge thought to engage the hair bundles of the inner hair cells (IHCs)
The thickness of the tectorial membrane in the apical coil of the Tectb−/− mutant was twice that of the heterozygous or wild type mice

notes.statement: Russell et al. (2007) found that Tectb-null mice had a low-frequency hearing loss below about 20 kHz, with reduced distortion product otoacoustic emissions in that range. At higher frequencies, neural sensitivity was close to normal, and basilar membrane and neural tuning were sharper than in wild-type mice. The authors attributed the sharper tuning to a reduced acting mass of the tectorial membrane and weaker longitudinal coupling along the cochlea.
quotes: Neural audiograms, based on the detection threshold of the compound action potential (CAP) recorded from the round windows of wild type and Tectb−/− mutant mouse cochleae, revealed a distinct low-frequency hearing loss in the Tectb−/− mutant mice.
Even with the highest levels of primaries used in these experiments, DPOAE levels in the frequency region below 20 kHz were 20–30 dB less than those recorded from wild type mice
These findings can be attributed to a reduction in the acting mass of the tectorial membrane and reveal a new function for this structure in controlling interactions along the cochlea.

notes.statement: Russell et al. (2007) concluded that Tectb is required to form the striated-sheet matrix of the tectorial membrane. Without Tectb, alpha-tectorin still formed disorganized filaments but not organized striated-sheet matrix, which suggested that Tectb may cross-link Tecta-based filaments.
quotes: indicating that Tecta can, in the absence of Tectb, form filaments but is unable to form organised striated-sheet matrix. Tectb is therefore essential for formation of the striated-sheet matrix and may act as a cross-linker of Tecta-based filaments.
